# t.must is an assert that stops the test where it fails; t.assert records
# the failure and goes on.
#
# The Go lowering answered only t.assert and wrote a comment for t.must, so a
# local read only by a must was declared and not used and the test program
# failed to build, and a must that held nothing passed. Kotlin's wrote the
# same comment, so android ran on past a failed must. html's agent assertTrue
# was fatal, so html stopped at a failed assert as at a must. Each runs
# verbose, which writes every failure the test logged.

! sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +3 tests, 2 failures'
stdout 'wanted 5, got 1'
! stdout 'wanted 3, got 1'
! sngl test -v --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +3 tests, 2 failures'
stdout 'must failed: \(s.N == 2\)'
stdout 'assert failed: \(s.N == 5\)'
! stdout 'assert failed: \(s.N == 3\)'
! sngl test -v --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +3 tests, 2 failures'
stdout 'must failed: \(s.N == 2\)'
stdout 'assert failed: \(s.N == 5\)'
! stdout 'assert failed: \(s.N == 3\)'
! sngl test -v --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +3 tests, 2 failures'
stdout 'must failed: \(s.N == 2\)'
stdout 'assert failed: \(s.N == 5\)'
! stdout 'assert failed: \(s.N == 3\)'
! sngl test -v --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +3 tests, 2 failures'
stdout '\(s.n === 5\)'
! stdout '\(s.n === 3\)'
! sngl test -v --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +3 tests, 2 failures'
stdout '\(s.n == 5\)'
! stdout '\(s.n == 3\)'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct S {
    n int
}

func testMustHolds(t test.Test) {
    var s = S{n=1}
    t.must(s.n == 1)
}

func testMustStops(t test.Test) {
    var s = S{n=1}
    t.must(s.n == 2)
    t.assert(s.n == 3)
}

func testAssertGoesOn(t test.Test) {
    var s = S{n=1}
    t.assert(s.n == 4)
    t.assert(s.n == 5)
}

ui.window {
    ui.text(value="x")
}
